definition: Yap Speech Cloud was a multimodal speech recognition system developed by American technology company Yap Inc.
details: It offered a fully cloud-based speech-to-text transcription platform that was used by customers such as Microsoft. The Company was a contestant at the inaugural TechCrunch conference and was subsequently acquired by Amazon in September 2011 to help develop products such as Alexa Voice Service, Echo, and Fire TV.
story: Picture a translator at the United Nations, listening to one language and whispering the meaning into another in real time. It figures out meaning by noticing which words like to travel together. It does not memorize a rulebook; it absorbs a library. Meaning lives in company — a word is known by the words it keeps. And that is Yap (company) — teaching a machine to read between the lines.
